title: Noctilucent Clouds over Sweden
explanation: Sometimes it's night on the ground but day in the air. As the Earth rotates to eclipse the Sun, sunset rises up from the ground. Therefore, at sunset on the ground, sunlight still shines on clouds above. Under usual circumstances, a pretty sunset might be visible, but unusual noctilucent clouds float so high up they can be seen well after dark. Normally too dim to be seen, they may become visible just after sunset during the summer when illuminated by sunlight from below the horizon. Noctilucent cloud s are the highest clouds and are known more technically as polar mesospheric clouds. Featured here as they appeared in early August, a network of blue noctilucent clouds was captured in the distant sky above a field of green grass near Linköping, Sweden, with trees in stark silhouette across the horizon. Much about noctilucent clouds has been discovered only in the past two decades, while how they form and evolve remains a topic of active research. Tomorrow's picture: round and round
credit: V. Höfer, D. Večerník & B. Večerníková

alt.title: Noctilucent clouds are pictured `above far western Kazakhstan
alt.description: iss074e0796136 (July 10, 2026) --- Noctilucent clouds—polar mesospheric clouds illuminated by sunlight just after the Sun has set below the horizon—are pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 267 miles above far western Kazakhstan. These high-altitude clouds are more easily seen from space than from the ground and form when extremely low temperatures freeze water vapor in the mesosphere during summer months at high latitudes. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams
